goal: Restore the generated MAUI/WinUI Windows entry point and manifest processing while keeping the migrated WinUI XAML classified correctly.
must_include: Says not to add a hand-written `Program.Main`; MAUI/WinUI should generate the Windows entry point when project items and the manifest are configured correctly.

Explains that `<EnableDefaultMauiItems>false</EnableDefaultMauiItems>` disables MAUI's default item globs, so the project must either restore defaults or explicitly include the Windows package manifest and classify MAUI XAML as `MauiXaml` versus native WinUI XAML as `Page`.

Uses the migration guidance properties deliberately, including `<UseMaui>true</UseMaui>`, `<UseWinUI>true</UseWinUI>`, Windows platform/runtime settings, and a valid `Package.appxmanifest` entry point of `$targetentrypoint$` when packaging.
Mentions the .NET MAUI multi-project template as a lower-friction alternative when a Windows-specific WinUI head has many native XAML pages.
must_not: Adds a console-style `static Main` to make CS5001 disappear.
Deletes the package manifest or sets `WindowsPackageType=None` without discussing whether the app is meant to be packaged.
Marks all XAML files as MAUI XAML when some are native WinUI `Page` files.
acceptable_alternatives: Re-enable default MAUI items and move native WinUI XAML into a separate Windows head project.
Create a new .NET MAUI Multi-Project App and compare its item groups/binlog with the migrated project.
Explicitly include `Platforms\Windows\Package.appxmanifest` as `AppxManifest` if default items remain disabled.
solved: The answer rejects a manual `Program.Main` and gives a coherent path: restore MAUI defaults, explicitly include/classify the manifest and XAML items, or move the Windows-native XAML into a MAUI multi-project Windows head.
partial: The answer avoids adding `Program.Main` but only mentions one of the item-glob/manifest problem or the multi-project alternative.
notes: The upstream issue remained nuanced, but the official migration document describes why default MAUI items may be disabled and what manifest changes a migrated WinUI project needs.
